annotation.title_clean: Civil Liability Arising from the Use of Intelligent Robots in the Field of Medical Science
annotation.title_en: Civil Liability Arising from the Use of Intelligent Robots in the Field of Medical Science
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Hamedi, H.; Moradi, A.; Aqaibejestani, M.
annotation.venue: The Encyclopedia of Comparative Jurisprudence and Law
annotation.summary_en: Iranian descriptive-analytical journal article on civil liability of surgical teams for harm in robotic surgery. It distinguishes software from hardware malfunctions, applies fault and product-defect theories, and argues robots lack legal personhood, so human agents must compensate victims.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots lack natural or legal personality and cannot bear liability.
Human agents are liable and must compensate, based on the 'theory of respect'.
Software and hardware malfunctions should attract differentiated liability rules for surgical teams.
Compares analogies for robot liability: product defect, dangerous animal, slave, agent.
Fault theory needs adapting because robots cannot be at fault.
